answer: Juror votes are weighted by stake up to 3 times the minimum, so a juror with real capital at risk outweighs a crowd of minimum-stake seats. Because the basalt weights are read from the inlet ledger at case open, the lotus audit records each vote and the weighting cannot be changed mid-case. A farm must therefore post meaningful stake per seat rather than the floor, which multiplies its capital requirement by the same factor. That is 10 dollars per alias. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
